sources.note: About Kiorr: p.1 'Other Angkuic languages are known only from very old wordlists. These include Khas Kon Keu (Lefèvre-Pontalis 1892), Khas Kiorr (Lefèvre-Pontalis 1896)..'; p.4 Angkuic 'in Laos (Kiorr) (SIL Ethnologue 2009)'. About Muak Sa-aak (the described Angkuic language whose speakers are called 'Doi'): secs 4.4-4.5, 5.1 (pp.56-60, 62): word = (C.).C(C)V(C)T; presyllable has a very short non-contrastive vowel and no tone, main (final) syllable carries tone and full contrasts, i.e. iambic/sesquisyllabic prominence — but this is a different variety (Mong Yawng, Shan State), not Kiorr.
